fact: ICASEES states the Central African Republic adopted its second national statistics development strategy (SNDS2, period 2024-2028, envelope of nearly FCFA 60 billion) in August 2023.

ICASEES held a workshop on 7-9 October 2026 in Bangui, with members of the statistical programming committee (CTPAS), to review implementation of SNDS2 2024-2028 at mid-term against its commitments, funded by UNDP.
ICASEES refers to the second national statistics development strategy (SNDS II) as being implemented in June 2026; no period or adoption date is given.
PARIS21's January 2026 NSDS status table lists the strategy as implementing (adopted): SNDS 2021-2025.
The 23 July 2026 ICASEES release says partners support the implementation of the national strategy for the development of statistics (SNDS); no period or adoption date is given.

At African Statistics Day in Bangui on 22 November 2024 the SNDS for 2024-2028 was presented, costed at 58 billion (currency not stated), of which 36 billion was available, with 0.15% of the state budget pledged to statistical activity.

ICASEES held a workshop on 18 July 2024 to update SNDS2, approved on 31 August 2023 for 2024-2028; its director general said the method requires the national statistical system's actors to meet each year to assess what worked the year before.
